loop.top3_series_pattern: trend_dominated with moderate seasonality and high predictability; unstable model ranking across windows
loop.top3_why: The mean combination of the full pool is the most robust strategy for a trend‑dominated series with unstable model rankings. It performs consistently across all three validation windows (0.6545, 0.6727, 0.6363) and avoids the high‑variance weight estimation that can overfit when only three windows are available. The DBA strategy, while slightly better in one window, shows a larger gap in the first window and is more sensitive to DTW alignment errors. The weighted strategy, although having the lowest overall score, relies on weights derived from a gradient‑boosted model trained on other series; with only three windows the weight estimates are noisy and may not generalize well to the blind test period.
loop.top3_why_not: B (DBA) has a larger first‑window error and is more sensitive to alignment noise, making it less reliable for a trend‑dominated series with unstable rankings. C (Weighted) achieves the best validation score but its weights are estimated from a limited sample (only three windows), leading to high variance and potential overfitting; the mean strategy offers a safer, more stable alternative.
